title: Role cartography: resource surface and delegation mapping
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Current RBAC surface at Redwood mixes coarse tenant-level roles and a handful of product-level privileges. As we roll out RBAC v2 for Private deployments and Dedicated tenants, we need a clear, explainable mapping from role semantics to the resource surface (clusters, deployments, routes, keys, models, billing) and a delegation model that supports scoped adminship, temporary elevation, and audited breakglass.

Goal: Produce a role model (roleset cartography) that: (1) enumerates resource domains and canonical scope identifiers, (2) defines composable role building blocks (capabilities) with least-privilege defaults, (3) specifies delegation/role-inheritance rules and temporal elevation flows, and (4) defines audit logging hooks and SSO/SAML group sync mapping required for safe rollout. Deliverables: design doc, permission matrix CSV, migration scripts plan, and test harness for explainability queries.
decision_rationale: We avoid a giant monolithic role-per-resource matrix. Instead we propose composable capability primitives (read, write, deploy, manage-keys, view-billing) bound to resource scopes (tenant, project, model, deployment). This enables smaller set of primitives that can be composed into curated roles and delegated across scopes. Temporal elevation implemented as time-limited role grants with audit token that records justification; breakglass flows require multi-actor approval for high-sensitivity scopes.
permission_matrix_summary: Permission matrix will be delivered as CSV with columns: capability, resource_domain, scope_pattern, default_role_bindings, risk_level, audit_required. Example rows: 'deploy','deployment','tenant:{id}/project:{id}/deployment:{id}','PlatformOperator,ProjectAdmin','high','true' ; 'read:logs','logging','tenant:{id}/**','SupportAgent,Viewer','low','true'. Matrix enforces machine-parseable scope patterns for runtime evaluation.
saml_sync_mapping: SSO groups map to curated rolesets rather than raw capabilities. Default mapping: SAML Group -> RoleSet name. We will support attribute-driven claims mapping (groups, department, title) and a fallback 'saml:unmapped' provisioned to a minimal onboarding role. Group-sync agent will include timestamped deltas to produce deterministic audit events for membership changes.
admin_controls: breakglass requires 2-person approval for scopes with risk_level=high
temporal elevation default TTL=1h, max TTL=24h by policy
immutable audit record for elevation and approval steps
tiered admin roles: Viewer, Operator, ProjectAdmin, PlatformAdmin, SecurityAdmin
self-service delegation limited to lower-sensitivity scopes (e.g., project-level) with audit trail
migration_plan: Phase 1: Inventory current roles and compute mapping heuristics to new capability primitives
Phase 2: Generate permission_matrix CSV and run dry-run evaluation against production ACLs (read-only) to surface drift
Phase 3: Offer opt-in rewrite for non-critical tenants with automated role translation
Phase 4: Enforce new evaluation during canary rollout for Dedicated and Private deployments
Phase 5: Full cutover with monitoring and rollback hooks
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of new signups + 2 pilot enterprise tenants on private deployment
Telemetry: compare allowed/blocked events and false-block rate over 7d
Fallback: runtime feature-flag to evaluate but not enforce for 48h windows
Communication: migration guide for SAML admins and CLI tooling for role inspection
open_questions: Which capabilities should be considered irreversible (e.g., delete-backed-up-keys)?
How do we present effective permissions to end-users in Console without leaking policy internals?
Do we require hardware-backed justification tokens (HSM) for breakglass in high-regulated tenants?
How should cross-tenant shared resources (marketplace models) expose scopes?
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Security and Product (comment threads resolved)
Permission matrix CSV validated against production ACLs with false-block rate <0.5% for baseline workloads
SAML group sync produces deterministic membership audit events visible in Console
Prototype evaluation library can compute effective permissions for arbitrary (actor, scope, action) queries and expose explainability strings for Console
